newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccon telecom sell-off would lure funds - expert.
newsitem.headline: Moroccon telecom sell-off would lure funds - expert.

text.p: Morocco will attract fund and portfolio foreign investors if it sends them a clear signal in privatising its telecommunications and speeding up a water concession with a French firm, a London-based consultant said on Tuesday.

David Pollock, from GMA Capital Markets in London, was speaking at a conference on the challenges facing Morocco in preparing its economy to compete in a free trade zone with the European Union by the year 2010.

"The privatisation of Itissalat al Maghrib (Morocco's telecommunications) would above all be a stong signal for direct and portfolio investors," Pollock told the conference attended by the country's economic leaders and businessmen.
A Moroccan parliamentary commission had begun debating a draft law aimed at privatising the telecommunications network to draw foreign investments.
Daewoo of South Korea, AT&T of the United States and Alcatel of France have shown interest in the privatisation of the GSM system, officials said.

Pollock also urged Morocco to speed up negotiations with the French firm Lyonnaise des Eaux on a 35 billion dirham ($3.8 billion) concession on taking over water and power distribution networks in Casablanca.
"To send clear signals to investors, it would be better that the negotiations with Lyonnaise des Eaux would be concluded and followed by other concession deals," he said in a report to the meeting.
The firm is negotiating with Casablanca authorities on the concession which has been criticised by some Moroccan businessmen who have said it would increase costs.
Morocco has earned over more than 10 billion dirhams from its privatisation programme which started in 1993.
Pollock said lack of liquidity on the Casablanca stock exchange was the key problem to attracting portfolio investment.
"The offering of privatisation, with an international tranche to buy into Itisslat al Maghrib's capital, will attract many funds managers who have not yet invested in Morocco," he said.
